correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=4, face classification gives X=U plus one relative triangle for each ground triple. The S_n-equivariant radial graph inclusion identifies H1(U;Z) with complete-graph cycles. With explicit oriented triangles, the connecting map is the standard integer simplex differential ∂2:Λ³Z^n→ker∂1. The boundaries of triples containing ground label 1 form a Z-basis of ker∂1 by an identity chord minor. Hence reduced homology is the integral kernel Λ³ker(ε), concentrated in degree 2. The exterior-power determinant identity establishes the character. All 5904 finite relabelings on n=4..7 satisfy signed simplicial Lefschetz checks, with direct simplicial Betti calculations modulo two and three; finite tests are ancillary.

originality.rationale: Linusson–Shareshian–Welker (arXiv:math/0410345, 2004) identify exactly the same complex as NM_2(n) and prove its non-equivariant sphere-wedge homotopy type in Theorem 1.1. Their Question 1.13 explicitly asks for the S_n-homology module of NM_k(n), which this finding resolves for k=2 integrally. Inspected full text including Section 4.1 does not determine the integral representation or trace. Barmak 2010 provides a separate nonequivariant proof, whereas stable Kneser, neighborhood and Cech results concern different complexes. Published indexed findings and accessible own claims were compared without locating a dominating integral S_n theorem. An unindexed later solution is a residual publication-priority risk.
residual_risks: The 2004 Question 1.13 may have been answered for k=2 in later unindexed literature. No decisive such source was found in targeted exact-alias, symmetric-group representation and indexed mathematical-record searches; publication priority remains provisional.
A full-text equivariant statement in unindexed or inaccessible literature might give an equivalent lattice.
The 2024 and 2026 related primary papers were compared by their publicly accessible abstracts, not their full bodies.

The general exterior-power identity is classical; originality is confined to its uniform integral realization for the ordinary Kneser independence complexes, not to exterior-power representation theory.

value.rationale: This completely determines a previously unspecified natural integral S_n-homology representation for an infinite canonical graph family (including the Petersen graph), not a small-parametric fact. It extracts the group action and integral lattice hidden by Barmak’s previously known sphere count, yielding a uniform hook Specht constituent, exact cycle-type character and vanishing global invariants. The integral lattice information is not implied by Betti numbers or the rational character; its structural role is intrinsic to equivariant topology of the family. The same S_n-module problem was posed explicitly as Question 1.13 by Linusson–Shareshian–Welker in 2004; the result resolves the first nontrivial matching-size case over Z, beyond their sphere-wedge count.
